description.narrative: Lund University (LU) serves as the academic partner to Trapca (Trade Policy Training Centre in Africa), a training center in Arusha, Tanzania, with the aim of strengthening LDC trade policy capacity through training, dialogue and networking. LU provides curricula and course outlines, provides part of the education/training and is responsible for examination and academic quality assuramce.

Lunds universitet (LU) fungerar som akademisk partner till Trapca (Trade Policy Training Centre in Africa, ett utbildningscenter i Arusha, Tanzania, med syfte att stärka MULs handelpolitiska kapacitet genom utbildning, dialog och nätverkande. LU står för kursupplägg, en del av utbildningen samt examination.

Lund University has been an academic partner to trapca. As the academic partner to ESAMI and trapca, LU is involved in the activities of trapca, contributes to and takes part in the various budget and reporting processes of trapca and has contributed also with inputs to the trapca completion report. LU appoints the Academic Director of trapca, who is part of the trapca management team and ex officio member of the trapca board. It is important to note that LU does not have an output of its own in the trapca project. lnstead, as a supporting institution LU has a share in the overall result of the centre. The overall goal of trapca's offering is poverty reduction through improved integration in the world economy of LDCs and low-income sub-Saharan countries through enhancement of capacity (knowledge and skills) to negotiate and implement pro-poor trade policies and trade laws. The programme objectives included: Developing trade policy skills by conducting short courses in trade policy and international trade negotiations.Having an internationally anchored Centre with both African and internationally reputable trade institutional linkages.Organising top-level thematic and topical conferences on trade policy and law.Developing and delivering, a Master of Science Progamme in Trade Policy and Trade Law. Creating an efficient and effective network of a community of African and international trade experts to serve as faculty members. Building human and physical infrastructure capacity adequately to meet programme quality and service delivery standards and expectations.

trapca's academic output during the period was well in line with the commitments made in the programme document and the centre has lived up to its guiding principles of academic excellence, African ownership, targeting of students from the poorest countries and striving towards gender balance. During the Consolidation Phase, Lund University contributed to the build-up of capacity at all levels at the Arusha office, exercising its quality control of trapca academic activities. This contribution took forms such as assistance in the build-up of e-learning facilities, fora and conferences, takíng active part in management decisions on a regular basis and providing suggestions for solutions to administrative and lT-related issues.

Cumulatively for the period under review, trapca was expected to attain 6000 participant weeks and this was in total exceeded by 2,330 participant weeks. There was also excellent performance among the students that participated in the advanced modules during the period under review as evidenced by an excellent average pass rate of 96 per cent.
